newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Stefanel well bought on prospects.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Stefanel well bought on prospects.

text.p: Italian textile group Stefanel saw another day of gains on the Milan bourse, at one stage suspended limit up, in what the company described as a "prize" by the market for the group's restructuring plan which envisages a return to the black this year.

"The 1996 balance sheet will show a huge improvement even though the results will still be negative," a Stefanel spokesman said, adding the company's "policy will be extremely cautious so as to see a positive 1997."
Stefanel categorically denied talk of a shareholding change or any eventual sell-offs. The company was studying some "important joint-ventures", the spokesman said without elaborating.
Stefanel stock, which touched a pre-suspension high on Monday of 1,621 lire, has posted a 27 percent gain since being quoted at 1,274 lire on January 21.
The company posted a first half 1996 pretax loss of 19.3 billion lire, against a 1.8 billion lire profit, on turnover of 251.3 billion lire, down 51.2 percent on the same 1995 half.
In February, the first shop resulting from Stefanel's joint-venture with U.S. designer Calvin Klein is due to open in Milan.
